scores.evidence: The prose is natural and uses です・ます throughout, with no 翻訳調 and no pressure phrases (hook-b1, s1-b5, s5-b1). One flashcard back, card-goal, has two noun-ending sentences in a row, which §1 does not allow.
lessons:lint --strict is clean, and every paragraph is short with one idea per sentence. The q4 explanation is the only paragraph with 4 sentences. It also uses 仕様書 before it defines it.

New terms are defined before use and stay within budget: 壁打ち, 目的・機能, MVP・MoSCoW and 1枚企画書・PRD each have a definitions block. Katakana and abbreviations get English on first use (ビジョン（vision）, MVP（Minimum Viable Product）, PRD（Product Requirements Document）). The glossary matches the text.

Every string has jp and en, and the two versions mean the same thing. The English reads naturally (q6, s2-b3 expect). The mermaid labels and alt text are localized and match the in-text names (今月の残り画面 / money-left screen).

mustFix.issue: (d) 3 sentences per paragraph (§1): the explanation has 4 sentences. It also uses 「仕様書」 in sentence 3 and explains it only in sentence 4.
mustFix.fix: 「Claude Codeの公式ガイド（Anthropic）も、役に立つ仕様書の特徴に、範囲外を書くことを挙げています。仕様書は、企画書のような文書です。」→「Claude Codeの公式ガイド（Anthropic）も、役に立つ仕様書（企画書のような文書）には範囲外を書く、としています。」

mustFix.issue: (d) です・ます, no consecutive 体言止め (§1): the card back is two noun-ending sentences in a row, 「…どうなれる」。」 and 「…手段。」.
mustFix.fix: 「目的は「誰が・どんな場面で・どうなれる」。機能はそのための手段。」→「目的は「誰が・どんな場面で・どうなれる」の形で書きます。機能は、目的を果たすための手段です。」

niceToHave: vibe-ch2 glossary (機能): two noun-ending sentences in a row, unlike s2-defs. Align it with the definitions block — 「目的を果たすための手段。アプリが「すること」。」→「目的を果たすための手段です。アプリが「すること」にあたります。」

ex-review / card-plan / q8: one set of headings is called 見出し, 項目 and 欄. 「項目」 also means data fields (「項目名だけ」), so use 見出し everywhere — 「6つの項目が1枚に並びます。」→「6つの見出しが1枚に並びます。」; 「1枚企画書の6項目」→「1枚企画書の6つの見出し」; 「画面の流れと扱うデータの欄だけが空です。」→「画面の流れと扱うデータの見出しだけが空です。」
q7 option c: SNS should be spelled out by its full name (§2) — 「SNS（ソーシャルメディア）」→「SNS（ソーシャル・ネットワーキング・サービス）」

ex-goal: the sample question differs from the one in s1-b4 expect. Reuse it so the learner sees the same exchange — 「「いつ困りますか？」には」→「「いまはどんな場面で困っていますか？」には」 (en: "When do you run into the problem?" → "When do you run into the problem today?")
s5-defs (MoSCoW): the reason for the name helps recall — 「機能をMust・Should・Could・Won'tの4つに分けて、優先順位を決める方法です。」→「Must・Should・Could・Won'tの頭文字から名づけられた、機能を4つに分けて優先順位を決める方法です。」
s5-b2 rows[0][1] (also ex-moscow expect and s2-b3 expect): the chain of の is heavy — 「今月の食費の予算の設定と残り金額の表示」→「今月の食費の予算を決めて、残り金額を表示する」 (change all three together).
summary: The Japanese is warm and natural, terms are introduced carefully, and the English versions match the Japanese closely. Two small rule breaks block the gate: the q4 explanation has 4 sentences in one paragraph, and the card-goal back uses two noun-ending sentences in a row. Both have exact replacements above, and lessons:lint --strict is already clean.
